Binding.description: What a symbol in a concept's name denotes.

meaning.description: One sentence saying what the symbol denotes; for a count, what it counts.

name.description: Display name of one to four words, e.g. "record length".

symbol.description:
The symbol in LaTeX, as it appears in the title's mathematics, without dollar signs,
e.g. `r` or `\kappa`.

quote.description: Text copied character for character from that source.

source.description: Id of the source the quote comes from.

oneOf.description: Show a claim by a method that splits it into sub-steps.
Infer one claim in a single step the sources report.

Motivation.description: Why a method suits the claim it shows.

quote.description: For an explicit motivation, the sources' words, copied exactly.

source.description: Whether the sources state the reason, leave it to be worked out, or neither.

text.description: The reason, in one or two sentences.

adds.description: Symbols the step introduces, in force in its sub-steps.

children.description: For a show step: its sub-steps, in the order the method takes them.

claim.description: What the step shows or infers, in one sentence, with mathematics in LaTeX ($...$).

deferred.description:
For an infer step the sources report out of order, before or after the steps around
it.

from.description:
Ids of the concepts the step relies on: known concepts, or pages before the step's
page.

id.description: A short label, unique in the tree, such as "S0" or "S2.1".

method.description:
For a show step: how the claim is shown, in a phrase ("reduce to a cyclic
convolution and bound its cost").

motivation.description: For a show step: why that method suits the claim.

page.description: Id of the page that presents this step and its sub-steps, if one does.

quote.description: For an infer step: the step as the sources report it, copied exactly.

salient.description:
For a step whose claim has a feature a reader would find striking (a symmetry, a
uniformity across cases, a surprising value or bound): that feature. The page should
explain why it holds, from a matching feature of the method.

oneOf.description: The sources state the reason; quote them.
The sources do not state it, but a reader can work it out from what they say.
The sources neither state it nor make it recoverable: you supply it.
The symbol denotes a thing: "ω, a primitive root of unity".

The symbol is the number of instances of something: "r, the number of complex
coefficients in a record".

root.description: The main step: to show the target result.
